Subject: Post-call recap: caching assumptions and pricing next steps

Thanks again for the time today, Alex — good conversation. Quick recap and action items so we have alignment before we update the proposal: 

1) Volume & behavior you shared:
- Primary use case: assistant for customer support agents (templates + retrieval + dynamic context)
- Expectation: ~300k agent sessions/mo initially, trending to 1.2M sessions/mo over 12 months
- Avg prompt+response per session: ~1.2 prompts, ~1.8K tokens/session on average (incl. history)

2) FastRetail constraints:
- Target monthly cloud budget for inference (starter): $12k - $20k / month; stretch to $35k/mo if latency and quality targets met
- Procurement: procurement team requires a clear per-1M-token effective price to budget for Q1

3) Key pricing levers we discussed:
- Model tier selection (better model = higher base $/1M tokens)
- Caching (prefix/shared prompt caching vs user-specific caches)
- Batching and request shaping

4) Ask from Redwood (what we'll need to finalize numbers):
- A realistic hit-rate range for caching given your reuse patterns (how often agents reuse templates / same retrieval keys)
- Confirmation of average session token distribution (system prompt vs dynamic retrieval vs generated tokens)

Next steps: Marcus will run a quick pricing sensitivity with 3 cache-hit scenarios and I’ll send an updated price sheet + worked examples. I attached the current pricing sheet and the MAP brief we referenced.

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this matches our notes. A few clarifications from our end: 

- Reuse patterns: agents use canned prompts (50-60% of starts) and paste a short customer summary or case id for retrieval. So expect higher hit rates on the initial template/prefix and much lower on end-of-session unique tokens.
- Token breakdown (approx avg 1.8K/session): system & template prefix ~300 tokens, retrieval/context ~400 tokens, generated response ~1.1K tokens.
- Budget: frontline teams can commit ~$12k/month initially; if effective cost per 1M logical tokens (after cache) is <= $25 we can look at faster ramp / larger pilots.

Looking forward to the worked examples. Alex

Alex — thanks for the quick clarifications. Below are the worked examples and assumptions we’ll use in the updated proposal. I kept the math simple so procurement can map to their budget.

Assumptions (for worked examples):
- Redwood list price (selected model): $35.00 / 1,000,000 billed tokens
- "Logical tokens" = the tokens your users experience (includes cached tokens)
- Cache hit-rate scenarios (applies to logical tokens): low = 15%, mid = 35%, high = 55%
- Prefix caching behavior: ~300 prefix tokens per session (templates + system prompt). Because many agents reuse templates, prefix hit applies disproportionately to the first ~300 tokens. Retrieval + generated tokens are less repeatable.

How we compute effective price per 1M logical tokens: 
- billed_tokens = logical_tokens * (1 - hit_rate)
- effective_price_per_1M_logical = list_price * billed_tokens_per_1M_logical
(where billed_tokens_per_1M_logical = (1 - hit_rate))

Worked examples (list price = $35 / 1M billed tokens):
- Low hit (15%): billed = 0.85M => effective = $35 * 0.85 = $29.75 per 1M logical tokens
- Mid hit (35%): billed = 0.65M => effective = $35 * 0.65 = $22.75 per 1M logical tokens
- High hit (55%): billed = 0.45M => effective = $35 * 0.45 = $15.75 per 1M logical tokens

Prefix-only vs full caching: 
- If prefix caching is the main mechanism (your case: templates reused a lot), you should expect hit rates higher for the first ~300 tokens and lower on the remaining ~1.5K tokens. Example: if prefix hit = 70% on the 300 prefix tokens, that saves 210 tokens/session (21% of the 1K+ response), translating to a net hit-rate on logical tokens of ~21% in that simplified example.
- Full-response or broader retrieval-key caching yields higher overall hit-rate (our mid/high examples), but requires stable retrieval keys or heavier canonicalization of prompts.

Implications for your budget:
- Using your numbers (1.2K sessions -> we’ll use the per-month totals you provided in the proposal): if your expected logical volume is 100M tokens/mo and you hit mid rate (35%), you would be billed for ~65M tokens. At $35/1M billed tokens that’s ~$2,275 => effective per-1M logical = $22.75 (matches the worked example). 
- If you want procurement-level clarity, we can show a 3-row table in the SOW with low/mid/high scenarios and the resulting monthly invoice estimates given your expected logical volume.

Next steps (proposed):
- Marcus: include the three hit-rate lines + ARR projection in the new pricing sheet (blocked for today)
- Marissa: send the versioned pricing sheet + SOW note that highlights caching assumptions and how we compute effective $/1M logical tokens (will attach to the proposal)
- Alex: if you can share any short sample of agent interactions (anonymized) or a breakdown of template reuse %, we can tighten the mid/high estimates and reduce procurement risk.

If this looks good I’ll push the updated sheet to HubSpot and share the link. Aim to have a proposal in your hands by EOD Fri.

Best,
Marissa
